newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ government moves to adjourn to February 18.
newsitem.headline: NZ government moves to adjourn to February 18.

text.p: The government on Friday moved a motion to adjourn parliament until February 18.
Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen was refused leave to set up select committees before Christmas.
Labour Leader Helen Clark amended the motion for the house to sit again on December 18 for the address-in-reply debate.
The debate follows the speech from the Governor-Genereal which outlines the government's programme.
By convention, it is the first opportunity for the opposition to test the government's mandate through a no confidence vote.
The debate will now be held when the house sits in February, if the government's motion succeeds.
